about.title: Buena Park Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Buena Park's workforce spans the entertainment and hospitality businesses along Beach Boulevard, warehouses and light manufacturing, and the delivery and service drivers who move between them. When someone gets hurt doing any of that work, the first question is usually simple: who pays for this? In California, workers' compensation normally covers medical care and a portion of lost wages regardless of who was at fault, and it is typically the only claim you can bring against your own employer. That is not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, a property owner, a defective piece of equipment, or another driver contributed to the injury, a separate third-party claim may be available. That matters for people injured in a work-related crash, too. Buena Park recorded 338 injury collisions in 2025, with 483 people hurt, and workers who drive for a living share SR-91, La Palma Avenue, and Western Avenue with everyone else. LawProactive connects you, free, with an independent attorney who can sort out which paths apply to your situation.

items.question: I was hit on SR-91 while driving for work in Buena Park. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were working, workers' compensation would typically cover your medical treatment and part of your lost wages no matter who caused the crash. If another driver was at fault, you may also have a separate third-party claim against that driver, which can cover losses workers' comp does not. An attorney can review the police report and explain how the two claims interact.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a workplace injury?
items.answer: No. Retaliating against an employee for reporting an injury or filing a workers' compensation claim is illegal in California. You should report the injury to your employer within 30 days to protect your benefits. If you experience pushback afterward, that is worth mentioning to the attorney you are connected with.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim against a third party after a work injury in Orange County?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally must be filed within two years of the injury. That deadline is separate from the workers' compensation process, which has its own reporting and filing rules. Because evidence at a job site or on a Buena Park roadway can disappear quickly, reaching out early gives an attorney more to work with.
